sermon.title: Father’s Day
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this Father’s Day message a guest speaker compares the birth of a baby with being born again, saying a baby has only two options, to be born and live or to die, and the same is true spiritually. He then follows Israel out of Egypt: Satan going after new believers through Pharaoh and the midwives, the lamb’s blood on the doorposts, and the hindrances after deliverance, including complaining, the flesh, emotions and fear. He closes with Jonah 2:9, “Salvation is of the Lord.”
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: the speaker is not named in the captions, and he refers to “Mr. Kincer” in the third person, so this appears to be a guest speaker rather than Pastor Kincer; the speaker line shows this and should be confirmed. He tells personal stories about his wife, young children and workplace, and names a church member and another man; those names appear only in the transcript. The captions for some references were written without colons and have been punctuated: “Psalms 82” is shown as Psalm 8:2, “Exodus 1:1” as Exodus 1:11 (the verse about the taskmasters), and “Exodus 1114” as Exodus 1:14. He cites “Exodus 6:13” where he speaks about accusing people when you have problems of your own; no matching passage is shown. His wording “ordained praise” in Psalm 8:2 differs from the NKJV, which reads “strength.” His words on taking a lamb and the hyssop come from Exodus 12:3–22 (he cites “Exodus 12:13”); the NKJV for 12:13 and 12:22–23 is shown. He makes personal and moral statements about sex outside marriage and abortion (about 18:00). “[Unclear]” marks three spots where the captions were not clear (in the first two minutes and near 39:00).

faqs.question: Why does he begin with a story about a baby being born?
faqs.answer: He describes the worry of the nine months and says “I was just glad they came out okay after all that.” He uses it to say a baby either is born and lives or dies, and the same is true spiritually.

faqs.question: How does he say a person is “conceived” spiritually?
faqs.answer: He says some people, when they hear God’s word, “it triggers a conception, and they begin to grow,” and the church continues that growth until they decide to accept Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus answered and said to him, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

faqs.question: Does he say God wants anyone to go to hell?
faqs.answer: No. He says “God doesn’t want any babies dying,” and that it happens “when we don’t accept him and let him birth us.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Jesus is the only one who can pay for sin?
faqs.answer: He says “the payment for your sin is death. Jesus Christ is the only one that has the power to pay for your sin,” and that he is “the only one that went down into hell, and hell couldn’t stand him.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by “the milk of the word”?
faqs.answer: He says it is “the basic understanding”: you “read the Gospels and find out about the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ,” which is “getting saved, faith, believing in God.”

faqs.question: What does he say about going to church every week?
faqs.answer: He says “It was a habit to be in the house of God on Sundays,” and asks, “what about Jesus’s custom?” He says “we need to be here at church.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

faqs.question: What does he say about babies and praise in the Psalms?
faqs.answer: He quotes “out of the mouths of babies” God has ordained praise to still the enemy, and says “This word means more than that.” He concludes that when we come to church “there’s no sitting down.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have ordained strength, Because of Your enemies, That You may silence the enemy and the avenger.

faqs.question: How did praising God help him as a new believer?
faqs.answer: He says “As a new believer, I was always praising God,” that he sang with all his heart whoever was next to him, and “that helped me in my life.”

faqs.question: What does he say about being embarrassed when we praise God?
faqs.answer: He says “it may be embarrassing,” but “That’s the great thing about kids,” who don’t care. For a teenager or adult with cares, “you just got to get rid of it.”

faqs.question: What does he say the “yoke of bondage” is?
faqs.answer: He says Galatians 5:1 is “the New Testament talking about, don’t be entangled with the yoke of bondage again, the yoke of sin,” and that “Sin is going to put you through the ringer.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Stand fast therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and do not be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.

faqs.question: What does he say children learn from their parents?
faqs.answer: He says “they’re going to copy the things that I do, no matter if they want to or not,” and later have to decide whether to reject what they saw.

faqs.question: What does he say about losing friends when you follow Christ?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s very difficult when friends don’t decide to follow Christ,” and that they may ask you “to leave, or they’re not going to associate with you anymore.”

faqs.question: What does he say happened at the Red Sea?
faqs.answer: He says “God destroyed the armies of Pharaoh,” who followed the Israelites after “He parted the Red Sea, the Israelites walked through it.”

faqs.answer: He quotes “Behold, I give you power to tread upon scorpions and serpents,” and says “He has the power to deliver us from sin.”

faqs.question: What does he say about Saul sacrificing before Samuel arrived?
faqs.answer: He says Saul “took things into his own hands” and went “outside of the pattern,” and that “We got to keep following the pattern.”
